extracted.intended_audience: general readers and performers interested in comedy genres, especially those researching or practicing clean/family-friendly comedy
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria for creating and performing 'clean comedy' — comedy generally free of explicit sexual content, profanity, and other objectionable material — including techniques, audience/venue suitability, and perceived quality markers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free from objectionable material
rubrics_metrics.description: Clean comedy is a comedy genre that is generally free of ribaldry: explicitly sexual content, profanity, politically or racially controversial jokes, toilet humor, and similarly objectionable material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the core definitional criterion. A routine should avoid explicit sexual language, profanity, jokes that are politically or racially controversial, toilet humor, and other material commonly considered objectionable if it is to be classified as 'clean comedy.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of indirect language and euphemism
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedians may try to circumvent clean-comedy restrictions by using innuendos, euphemisms, doublespeak, double entendres, and gender-neutral language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are acceptable craft techniques for producing clean material: imply rather than state, choose less explicit wording, or use wordplay/double meanings to get laughs while remaining within 'clean' boundaries. The article notes these techniques let performers stay clean while still being clever or provocative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed provocation (not necessarily unprovocative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clean comedy is not necessarily unprovocative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoiding explicit or obscene content does not require blandness; material can still provoke thought or strong reactions. Performers can push boundaries of subject matter or viewpoint without resorting to profanity or sexual explicitness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skill / difficulty as an evaluative marker
rubrics_metrics.description: Getting laughs from clean material 'is harder' and some consider clean comedy to be a higher form of comedy than bits that rely on profanity or sexual content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ability to elicit laughs without shock tactics is framed as an indicator of craft — tight writing, strong setups and punchlines, and inventive word choice are emphasized. Quotes from practitioners (e.g., Bob Newhart) are cited to support this evaluative standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vulgarity as a potential sign of weak material
rubrics_metrics.description: Many who rely on dirty humor do so because vulgar language helps sell weak jokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presence of profanity or vulgarity can be used as an evaluative heuristic: if obscenity is required to get a laugh, the underlying joke or premise may be structurally weak.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience and venue suitability / broad appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Clean comedy appeals to the largest possible audience and advertisers; it is suited for corporate conferences, cruise ships, non-profit organizations, schools and churches, and family-friendly entertainment contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When crafting material for these venues, prioritize universality, inoffensiveness, and avoidance of controversy. Broadcast constraints (e.g., FCC rules against obscenity) historically encouraged clean material; consider regulatory and sponsor sensitivities when evaluating suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical focus and subject matter choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Clean comedians often focus their bits on everyday things like food and raising children (examples: Jim Gaffigan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose relatable, observational topics (family life, food, daily annoyances) that naturally lend themselves to humor without explicit content. This subject-matter strategy supports broad appeal and reduces risk of offending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market and platform considerations for distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: There are outlets and markets that specifically support clean comedy (e.g., CleanComedians.com, Dry Bar Comedy, Studio C) and these channels can attract large audiences for clean routines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing clean material, target platforms and booking rosters that specialize in or value family-friendly content. This affects decisions about tone, pacing, and promotional strategy.
